sections.heading: Water on the Floor and No Number to Go With It
body: It's Saturday morning. There's water on the basement floor, you've found the main and shut it off, and you're standing there with your phone. The first plumber you call can look at it next week, and will give you a price after that.
So you wait with the water off. No dishwasher, no shower, and no idea whether this is a small valve or a big job.
The wait is bad. Not knowing what it'll cost is worse.

sections.heading: What We Get Called For
body: Most plumbing calls start with something small that got ignored. Here is what we're usually asked to look at.

items.title: A drain that won't clear
items.text: Kitchen sinks, tubs, floor drains and the line out to the street. We clear it, and tell you what's making it back up.

items.title: A leak you can't find
items.text: A stained ceiling, a wet basement wall or a water bill that jumped. We track down where the water is coming from before anyone cuts into a wall.

items.title: A water heater that's quit
items.text: No hot water, or a puddle under the tank. We repair and install tank and tankless heaters, gas or electric.

items.title: A faucet, toilet or shower that's failing
items.text: A drip, a toilet that keeps running, or a bathroom that needs a new shower. Repaired when that's enough, replaced when it isn't.

items.title: A gas line
items.text: New lines and repairs, for homes and for businesses.

items.title: A sewer line
items.text: Slow drains throughout the house, gurgling, or a backup in the lowest drain. We find out whether it's a clog or a broken line.

sections.heading: Saturday and Sunday Calls
body: Pipes don't wait for Monday. We've come out on Saturdays and on Sundays, and we'll tell you when we can be there while you're on the phone or texting.
Start your message with what's happening and where your shutoff is. If the water is still running, shut it off first and then call.

sections.heading: The Job Isn't Done When We Leave
body: A plumbing fix is only as good as how it holds up the next week. Our residential plumbing work comes with a one-year guarantee, and drain cleaning with six months.
If something acts up after we've gone, call the same number. We'd rather hear from you than have you wonder.

sections.quote: Reliable and professional. How many people do you know that actually call and verify how their work is performing a week after it was done? I will always call this plumbing company before anyone else!
sections.name: Stazia G.

sections.heading: Homes, Rentals and Businesses

We do residential and commercial plumbing, from kitchen drains to public restrooms and backflow testing. Commercial work carries its own guarantee terms, so ask when you call.

sections.quote: Emergency drain clog in my commercial building. Up to Code handled it quickly and communicated the problem and solution well.

items.a: Call (316) 400-7586 or text (316) 333-5434 and tell us what's happening. We'll tell you when we can be there. We've come out on Saturdays and Sundays, so don't wait for Monday if water is running.

sections.heading: What Happens When You Call About a Sewer Problem
body: Tell us what the drains are doing and which ones. Text a photo to (316) 333-5434 if you can, or call (316) 400-7586. We tell you what we think is going on.
From there we work out whether it's a clog we can clear or a line that needs repair. If we need to look inside the pipe, we say so and explain why.
You hear what we think and what it should cost before you agree to the visit. Then you decide.

image.alt: Floor drain in a basement utility room

sections.heading: Signs the Problem Is in the Sewer Line
body: A single slow sink is usually a clog in that sink's own pipe. When the trouble shows up in more than one place, the main line is the first thing to suspect.
If any of these sound familiar, don't keep running water and hope.

items.title: More than one drain is slow
items.text: The tub, the washer drain and a toilet all act up on the same day. One shared line is the likely cause.

items.title: Gurgling when something else runs
items.text: The toilet bubbles when the washer drains. Air is being pushed through a line that isn't moving water freely.

items.title: Water in the lowest drain
items.text: A basement floor drain or the lowest tub fills when a fixture upstairs runs. That's the line backing up.

items.title: A sewage smell
items.text: A smell near a floor drain or in the yard points to a problem in the line or a failed seal.

items.title: Wet or sunken ground
items.text: A soggy patch in the yard, or ground that has dropped along the path of the line, can mean a break.

sections.quote: Ken came in and did an outstanding job on replacing all the drain plumbing on my new house I just bought. Very cordial and communicated very well.
sections.name: Jacob G.

sections.heading: Clog or Broken Line?
body: A clog can usually be cleared. A broken, shifted or root-filled pipe needs a repair, and clearing it only buys time.
That difference matters because the two jobs cost very different amounts. We'd rather tell you which one you have than sell you the bigger job.
Drain cleaning is its own service, with a six-month guarantee on residential work. If your problem turns out to be a clog, that's what you'll get.

sections.heading: A Look Inside Before the Repair
body: Camera inspections are part of our sewer service. Looking inside the line shows what is actually there, instead of guessing from the symptoms.
It's most useful when drains keep backing up after being cleared, when you've just bought an older house, or when you're deciding whether to repair a section or replace more of the line.

sections.heading: Repair a Section or Replace the Line?
body: Damage that's limited to one section is a smaller job than a line that's failing along its length. The right answer depends on what the pipe looks like inside and how much of it has a problem.
We tell you what we found, lay out the options, and you decide. We don't have a price to give you here, because it depends on the line, and we won't guess.

sections.heading: While You Wait for Us
body: A few things help if the line is backing up. None of them replace a plumber, and all of them keep a bad day from getting worse.

items.title: Stop running water
items.text: Skip the dishwasher, the washer and long showers until we've looked at it.

items.title: Don't keep flushing
items.text: If the toilets are slow or bubbling, flushing again can push more water into the lowest drain.

items.title: Note which drains are affected
items.text: It tells us whether the trouble is at one fixture or in the main line.

items.title: Send a photo
items.text: A floor drain, a wet spot or whatever you're seeing. Text it to (316) 333-5434 with a line about what's happening.

sections.heading: Homes, Rentals and Buildings
body: We work on sewer and drain problems at houses, rentals and commercial buildings. Tell us what kind of property it is when you call, and who we should meet there if it isn't you.

items.q: Can I text you a photo of the problem?
items.a: Yes. Text it to (316) 333-5434 and add a line about what's happening. Or call (316) 400-7586 and tell us.

items.q: How do I know if it's a clog or a broken line?
items.a: If one drain is slow, it's often a clog. If several drains are slow, gurgle or back up together, the main line is the likelier cause. Tell us what you're seeing and we'll say what we think.
Yes, camera inspections are part of our sewer service. We use them to see what's wrong inside the line before a repair.
Yes. Drain cleaning is one of our main services, and residential drain cleaning comes with a six-month guarantee.

items.q: Can you come on a weekend?
items.a: We've come out on Saturdays and Sundays. Call or text and we'll tell you when we can be there.

items.q: Do you work on commercial buildings?
items.a: Yes. We do commercial plumbing as well as residential, including drain cleaning and backflow testing.

sections.heading: What We Install and Replace
body: Fixtures are the parts of your plumbing you touch every day, and they're usually the first to wear out. We install and replace these in kitchens and bathrooms.

items.title: Faucets
items.text: Kitchen and bathroom faucets, and outdoor faucets that have failed. A photo of the old one, with the brand if you can see it, helps.

items.title: Toilets
items.text: A toilet that runs, rocks, leaks at the base or won't flush well. We tell you whether a repair is enough or the toilet should go.

items.title: Showers and tubs
items.text: Shower valves, showerheads and full shower enclosures, including the supply pipes behind them.

items.title: Sinks
items.text: Kitchen and bathroom sinks, with the drain and supply lines under them.

sections.quote: Ken did a great job with installing our shower enclosure and fixing our old corroded pipes. When I called, I was always able to talk to Ken and he was the one that did the service. An outstanding job for a much needed update!
sections.name: Marla W.

sections.heading: Repair It or Replace It?
body: A worn washer or a bad cartridge is a small repair, and the faucet keeps going. A fixture with a cracked body, heavy corrosion or parts that can't be found is another story.
Here's a rule you can check yourself. If the fixture works most of the time and one part is failing, repair it. If it's leaking from the body or you're fixing it every few months, replace it.
We tell you which side you're on, and what each costs, before we start.

sections.heading: Why a Toilet Keeps Running
body: A toilet that runs on its own wastes water and usually has a short list of causes. Most are small parts inside the tank, not the toilet itself.

items.title: A worn flapper
items.text: The rubber seal at the bottom of the tank stops sealing, and water seeps into the bowl all day.

items.title: A tired fill valve
items.text: The valve that refills the tank doesn't shut off cleanly, so water keeps trickling in.

items.title: A cracked bowl or tank
items.text: This one isn't a part. If the porcelain is cracked or leaking at the base, it's time for a new toilet.

sections.heading: What's Under the Fixture
body: Swapping a faucet or a toilet is a good time to look at the shutoff valves and supply lines beneath it. Old ones that stick or weep are worth replacing while the fixture is out.
The same goes for pipes. If we see corrosion or a fitting that's seeping, we tell you what we see. You decide whether to handle it now or later.

sections.quote: Ken replaced two outdoor faucets that had frozen during the winter. The access was limited and inside a crawlspace. He was friendly, professional and had the whole job knocked out in under two hours. The price was great and he earned a new customer for any of our future plumbing needs.
sections.name: Tom O.

sections.heading: Outdoor Faucets and Winter
body: An outdoor faucet can split when water freezes inside it, and you often don't find out until spring, when it sprays inside the wall.
Disconnecting hoses before the first hard freeze helps. If a faucet drips after winter, or water shows up inside the wall behind it, call us.

sections.heading: Before You Call
body: If you can do it safely, find the small shutoff valve under the fixture and turn it off. For a toilet, the valve is on the wall or floor behind it.
If water is spraying and you can't stop it, shut off the main water valve for the house, then call. A photo of the fixture and the shutoff is the fastest way to start.

items.q: Can I text you a photo of the fixture?
items.a: Yes. Text it to (316) 333-5434 with a line about what's wrong, or call (316) 400-7586.

items.q: Do you install fixtures I bought myself?
items.a: Ask when you call. Tell us what it is and where it's going, and we'll tell you what we can do.

items.q: Can you repair a faucet instead of replacing it?
items.a: Often, yes. We'll tell you whether a repair is enough or the faucet should be replaced.

items.q: Do you do bathroom and kitchen fixtures both?
items.a: Yes. We work on faucets, toilets, showers and sinks in kitchens and bathrooms.

items.q: What if the new fixture leaks?
items.a: Call us. Our residential plumbing work comes with a one-year guarantee.

footer.about: Up To Code Plumbing is a Wichita plumbing company run by Ken Carrick. It handles drains, leaks, sewer lines, water heaters, fixtures and gas lines for homes and businesses.
why: Text a photo and ask the price

On a phone, your current site is laid out about 980 pixels wide on a 390 pixel screen. The header buttons print over each other and the hero text is cut off at the edge. Most people searching for a plumber are on a phone, and they have to scroll sideways to read you.

Your reviews describe a plumber who will price a job from a text. George A. texted you a photo and got a fair quote right away, when another local company wanted a visit first. Today those words sit on Google, not on your site, and the text line is mentioned only on your booking and Augusta pages.
So the demo tells one story everywhere: send a photo, ask the price, decide. It opens with plumber in Wichita, KS, and gives sewer line repair and fixture installation a page each.
